mainEntity.name: Do you need a separate heating and cooling system for an in-law suite addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Depending on the size and cooling capacity of your current air conditioner, tying into the primary unit may overextend the system and cause uneven temperatures. In many cases, installing an independent ductless mini-split system is the most efficient solution for a multigenerational suite. A mini-split allows extended family members to control their own room temperature without altering the rest of the house, while avoiding the major expense of replacing your primary central HVAC unit.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not always, but adding a ductless mini-split is often the best choice for providing independent temperature control without overloading your home's main HVAC system.
